key_insight: The paper introduces MSVR, a variance-reduction estimator that tracks multiple coupled inner functions using only one sampled block per iteration, enabling efficient optimization for finite-sum compositional problems.
engineering_relevance: This improves the practicality of large-scale stochastic optimization in settings where full inner-function access is too expensive, such as multi-task learning and deep AUC maximization.
method: Multi-block-Single-probe Variance Reduction (MSVR) tracks the vector g(w) across m blocks with partial block sampling.
Builds FCCO algorithms for non-convex, convex, strongly convex, and PL objectives.
Obtains better sample complexity, with improved m-dependence when outer gradients are linear.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improved theoretical sample complexities and empirical gains on multi-task deep AUC maximization.
watch_item: Performance depends on stochastic access to inner functions and block-sampling design, so estimator stability and implementation overhead may matter in practice.
paper_title: Solving Finite-sum Coupled Compositional Optimization via Multi-block-Single-probe Estimator
